- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak or adjust downward by 3–8% in next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “lag correction” by reducing first 5 days’ forecast by 1–3%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversals” (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
